messages:
lena: quick sync 1024 7: we need a final pattern for validation on the new pipeline config form. It's long, paginated, and some blocks are optional. inline validation vs on-submit vs progressive summary?

ben: leaning progressive: lightweight inline hints while users type (non-blocking), and an explicit per-step summary when they try to advance or submit. Keeps noise down but still actionable.

mika: agree with progressive. also we should avoid immediate red on first keystroke. validate on blur or after a short debounce (500ms) for async checks like name uniqueness.

sam: accessibility: errors must be programmatically related to the field (aria-describedby), and the summary should be a real list with links/anchors to each invalid field. For screen reader users a single summary readout is useful.

lena: for optional collapsed sections, proposal: show a compact error pill on the collapsed header like "1 issue" and expand-on-click. on submit expand the first collapsed section with errors. avoid auto-focusing inside it to keep tab flow sane.

ben: copy idea for the step banner: "Step 2 of 4 — 2 items need attention" rather than "errors". softer tone and clearer about scope. we can show a red dot + count icon.

mika: required markers: i propose using explicit inline label when space allows: e.g., "API key (required)". for compact lists we can use an asterisk but include visible helper text for screen readers. avoid asterisks that only rely on color.

sam: microcopy alternatives for the global summary: 1) "Please address the following to continue." 2) "Some items need attention before you can proceed." 3) "Fix the highlighted fields to move on." Which is best?

lena: #1 is clear and action-oriented. short and direct.

ben: animation/UX nit: when the step summary scrolls into view on mobile, keep the motion subtle and don't steal focus. users should be able to keep typing.

mika: error density: if a step has >5 validation issues, collapse the list under a "Show all" toggle and surface the top 3 most common problems. prevents overwhelm.

sam: testing checklist: keyboard-only navigation, screen reader readout of the banner & list, mobile behavior for sticky step CTA, collapsed-block indicators, and blur/debounce timing for inline checks.

lena: destructive action at the end: we have "Remove pipeline and artifacts (permanent)". thoughts on guardrails? typed-confirm, modal confirm + undo, or inline toggle?

ben: proposal: three-tier rule: reversible items -> modal + toast with undo (soft-delete backend required); irreversible customer data -> modal with typed-confirm and explicit consequences; bulk-power actions triggered by API -> require role-based confirmation + typed-confirm.

mika: agree. typed-confirm text should be explicit and include exact name: "Type REMOVE to permanently delete 'Pipeline-42'". keep the input clear and provide a copy button for long names.

sam: accessibility: typed-confirm dialogs must trap focus, announce their purpose via aria-labelledby, and expose the typed value to assistive tech only when requested. avoid relying on color contrast alone for error state.

lena: developer constraints: undo needs soft-delete & background worker to finalize. if infra can't ship immediately we'll spec modal + irreversible notice now and mark undo as Phase 2.

ben: rollout plan: Phase A - progressive validation (blur + debounce) + per-step summary banners + explicit required labels. Phase B - collapsed-section pills + expand-on-submit + error anchor links. Phase C - typed-confirm rules and undo backend.

mika: acceptance criteria: 1) keyboard & SR flows pass, 2) step banner is present & counts update on validation, 3) collapsed headers show issue pills, 4) irreversible delete uses typed-confirm, 5) undo implemented or clearly scheduled.

sam: i'll add an accessibility checklist to the RFC and mock up the ARIA attributes we should use.

lena: great. ben & mika will add Figma screens for progressive vs on-submit variants. i'll draft the RFC with the phased plan and ship acceptance criteria.

aria-bot: reminder: include automated tests for ARIA live region announcements and ensure color contrast >= 4.5:1 for error text.

ben: thanks all. will post Figma links in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
